config.title: Berlin Bulky Waste - FAQ
config.subtitle: What a recycling yard takes free, why an over-size load is refused whole, what a booked collection costs, where rubble and paint have to go instead, and the fine for leaving it outside.

items.q: How much does bulky waste cost in Berlin?
items.a: It depends on whether you drive it or have it collected. **Driving it to a BSR recycling yard is free up to 3 m³ of bulky waste per vehicle.** A collection from your door is **€50 for up to 5 m³ on the saver fee**, collected from the sixteenth working day, or **€100 for up to 5 m³ on the standard fee**, collected inside fifteen working days. Above 5 m³ each further started cubic metre adds €10 on the saver fee and €20 on the standard fee.

items.q: What counts as bulky waste at a Berlin recycling yard?
items.a: Old furniture, plus **scrap wood, scrap metal and hard plastics, which all count together as one waste type** against the same 3 m³ allowance. Mixed building and demolition waste does not count and is not accepted at all. Upholstered furniture has one exception: a full suite over 3 m³ can still be unloaded, and you may bring one further cubic metre of bulky waste with it.

items.q: What happens if my load is bigger than 3 cubic metres?
items.a: **The yard refuses the whole load, not the excess.** Partial unloading is not allowed, so you cannot drop three cubic metres and drive one home. BSR's own worked example is a delivery of four cubic metres of bulky waste plus a fridge: the fridge is accepted as an electrical appliance and the bulky waste is turned away. Your options above the line are a booked collection, the sorting plant at Gradestraße 81 at €180 a tonne with a €72 minimum, or the Saturday counter at the Gradestraße yard, which takes 3 to 5 m³ for a flat €180 paid before you unload.

items.q: Where do I take an old fridge, washing machine or television?
items.a: **Any BSR recycling yard, free, in household quantities and with no volume limit.** Electrical appliances are never counted against the 3 m³ bulky waste allowance, and a booked collection takes them along free as well. Take out the batteries where you can and tape the poles, because a shorted lithium cell can start a fire in the container. Shops are the other route: a retailer with **at least 400 m² of electrical sales floor**, or a supermarket over 800 m² that sells electricals regularly, has to take back a comparable old device when you buy a new one, and must take small devices **no larger than 25 cm on any side** free of charge without any purchase at all, up to three per device type.

items.q: Can I put tiles and renovation rubble in with the furniture?
items.a: No, and it is the expensive part of any renovation. **Mineral rubble costs €4 per started 10 litres, which is €400 a cubic metre**, and there is no free allowance. **A booked collection will not take it at any price**, so rubble always has to be driven. Mixed building and demolition waste is refused at the yard outright. Bagged household and renovation waste is separate again at **€3 per started 50 litres, up to 500 litres**.

items.q: Where do old paint, solvents and weedkiller go?
items.a: To a hazardous waste counter, and **only five of the fourteen Berlin yards have one**. For a Berlin private household it is **free up to 20 kg per waste type per day**, and above that the rates run from €1.30 a kilo for old oil and medicines to €6.40 for chemicals. Unlike bulky waste, partial unloading is allowed here. Household batteries, car lead batteries, fluorescent tubes, energy-saving lamps and LEDs are free at every yard, not only the five.

items.q: What is the fine for leaving furniture on the street in Berlin?
items.a: Berlin's fine catalogue for environmental offences, published in the official gazette on 14 November 2025, sets **€300 to €1,500 for a single small item** such as a mattress, suitcase or chair, **€1,500 to €4,000 for several small items or one larger one** such as a wardrobe, bed frame or bathtub, **€4,000 to €8,000 once the pile reaches a cubic metre or 100 kg**, and **€8,000 to €11,000 above that**. Anything with hazardous parts, so a fridge, television, boiler, washing machine, fluorescent tube or phone, sits in its own band of **€1,000 to €15,000** whatever it measures.

items.q: Can a friend or a man with a van take it to the yard for me?
items.a: A friend can, a commercial hauler cannot. The acceptance conditions say household waste has to be delivered **by the person who produced it or by a private third party such as a neighbour, friend or relative**, using a private car or any hired or borrowed vehicle. Other transporting parties are not allowed to deliver household waste at a yard. The **limits also count per vehicle rather than per person**, so two of you in one car still share one 3 m³ allowance.

items.q: Do I need to prove I live in Berlin?
items.a: Only Berlin waste is accepted. Anyone delivering from outside Berlin has to prove the waste came from Berlin, which is normally done with the original ID card of the person the waste belongs to. Nothing is weighed at a yard: staff estimate the volume by eye, and their rule of thumb is that **a full Multivan boot is about 3 m³**.
